draft.title: Causes of exclusion
card: Social exclusion is being shut out of work, services, decisions or social life. Many different things can cause it, and often more than one acts at once.
Poverty
a low income can make it hard to pay for transport, internet, fees or social activities, so a person may miss out.
Disability and discrimination
a building without ramps can shut out a person who uses a wheelchair. Unfair treatment because of race, gender, religion or age can shut people out of jobs or housing.
Location, age and education
people in remote areas may live far from services. Young and older people may be left out of decisions or jobs. Low literacy or few qualifications can limit access to work.
draft.remember: Exclusion has many possible causes, and a person can face several at once.

a.q: A town has no bus service and the nearest clinic is 200 km away. Which cause of exclusion does this show best?
a.why: Distance from services is a feature of where people live, so location is the cause. Discrimination is tempting, but nothing here describes unfair treatment of a group of people.
a.clue: Think about where the town sits, not who lives there.

b.q: Leon, 17, lives in a remote community. His family has a low income, so they cannot afford home internet. He cannot do online TAFE courses. Which statement is best?
opts: Location and poverty together limit his access to learning
Only his age explains why he cannot take part
Disability is the main cause of his exclusion
Poverty is the only cause, as location has no effect
b.why: Remote living and a low income both limit Leon's access, and the card says causes can act together. Poverty alone is tempting, but the remote location also shapes what he can reach.
b.clue: Look for more than one cause in the story.

b.best: Location and poverty together limit his access to learning

problems.detail: The first bullet defines social exclusion ('being shut out of work, services, decisions or social life'), which belongs to point 1 and should only be mentioned here.

Two distractors use 'only' ('Only his age explains...', 'Poverty is the only cause...'), so the right option stands out as the only balanced, multi-cause statement. A student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Look for more than one cause in the story' gives the answer away, because only one option names more than one cause.

The story says the family cannot afford home internet because of low income, and the courses are online. It never shows how the remote location limits his access, such as poor coverage or no nearby campus. So the 'location' half of the answer, and the why's claim that location 'shapes what he can reach', is not supported by the scenario.

check.summary: Both questions have clear right answers, but question b gives its answer away through 'only' distractors and a clue pointing to more than one cause, and its scenario does not show how location limits Leon. The card also re-defines exclusion, which belongs to point 1.

b.q: Leon, 17, lives 300 km from the nearest TAFE campus, with no phone coverage. His family's low income means they cannot pay for satellite internet or travel. Which two causes best explain why he cannot study?
b.why: The distance and lack of coverage come from where he lives, and the cost of internet and travel comes from low income. Lack of education is tempting, but missing out on TAFE is a result of his situation here, not what causes it.
b.clue: Ask what stops him reaching the course, not what he misses.
